pages.title: How many moons does Jupiter have? (2026 count)
pages.text:
# How many moons does Jupiter have?
Jupiter has 115 confirmed moons as of 2026, the second most of any planet after Saturn. The count is officially recognized by the International Astronomical Union.
## The big four
The four largest, the Galilean moons, are Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto, discovered by Galileo in 1610.
## Why the number keeps changing
Most of Jupiter's moons are small irregular moons a few kilometres across, found by large telescopes since 2000. New discoveries are announced most years, so the total keeps rising.
## Summary
- Confirmed moons: 115
- Largest: Ganymede
- Most volcanic: Io

pages.text:
# How long to boil an egg
Bring water to a rolling boil, lower large eggs in gently, then time them:
- 6 minutes: runny yolk, set white
- 8 minutes: jammy yolk
- 10 minutes: firm but still bright yolk
- 12 minutes: fully hard-boiled
Move the eggs to ice water for 5 minutes to stop the cooking and make peeling easier. Add a minute for extra-large eggs and take off a minute for medium eggs. At high altitude, add 1 to 2 minutes.

pages.title: How to boil an egg perfectly
pages.text:
Boiling an egg well is all about timing. A large egg needs about 10 minutes for a firm yolk.
## 1. Bring water to a boil
Fill a pot with enough water to cover the eggs and bring it to a rolling boil.
## 2. Lower the eggs in
Use a spoon so they don't crack.
## 3. Time them
6 minutes for runny, 8 for jammy, 10 for firm, 12 for fully hard-boiled.
## 4. Cool them
Move the eggs to ice water for 5 minutes.
## 5. Crack and roll
Tap the shell all over and roll the egg gently.
## 6. Peel
Start at the wide end where the air pocket is.

pages.text:
# What is the capital of Australia?
The capital of Australia is Canberra, in the Australian Capital Territory. It is not Sydney or Melbourne, as many people assume.
## Why Canberra?
When the colonies federated in 1901, Sydney and Melbourne both wanted to be the capital. As a compromise, a new city was built between them. Canberra was chosen in 1908 and Parliament first met there in 1927. It was designed by the American architects Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin.
